author: AlexGFU
text:
What @PaydRH built is a routing layer, not a new market.

$PONS already takes a creator fee. 

@RobinhoodCrypto already issued $SPCX $NVDA $QQQ $SPY and $TSLA as ERC-20s. $PAYD's move is pointing the fee at a contract that buys those tokens and pushes them to holders.

That is a real product idea: give a launch a reason to be held that is not “maybe the chart goes up.”

No staking is the right UX for that.

Will it stick on Robinhood Chain? As infrastructure, it can. The chain was built for tokenized stocks, $PONS is already a native launch venue, and $PAYD does not need Robinhood’s permission to be a fee recipient. That is the whole integration.

What can kill it is not “Robinhood bans $PAYD.” It is $PONS losing launch flow, Stock Tokens getting paused or illiquid, or creators deciding they’d rather take the fee in $ETH than give it to holders.

The protocol sticks if enough launches keep pointing fees at vaults. The $PAYD token sticks only if that flow is large and people price the token as a claim on it.

The basket of RWAs help marketing more than it determines whether the machine works.

If the basket were random mid-caps nobody recognizes, the same contracts would still run and almost nobody would care. So names matter for adoption. They do not matter for solvency of the loop. The loop lives on volume.

A better basket makes people want to launch through it. Volume is what actually buys the stocks.

Two different bets, then:

author: oct_gems
text:
Could @TradePools be the next $PONS?

Or is it simply the Pons of Arc, without a token to capture the upside?

Yesterday, Pools confirmed it will be a day-one launchpad on @arc. 

That matters because PONS already proved what happens when one launchpad becomes the center of activity on a new chain.

Pons did more than launch tokens on Robinhood Chain. It became the place where new tokens were created, traded and discovered. 

More launches created more volume, more fees and more PONS burns.

Now Pools gets to test the same idea on Circle’s new USDC-native L1.

But the product itself is very different.

Pools is built by @Uniswap Labs and launches tokens directly into Uniswap v4 pools from day one.

The fee is 0.25%, far below the roughly 1% charged by many launchpads. Liquidity is locked, fees compound back into the protocol-held LP position, and creators cannot simply pull the liquidity.

There are also two launch modes.

Instant Launch lets creators go live immediately, while Crowd Launch uses a 4-hour TWAP designed to reduce the advantage of snipers and bundled launches.

Once the token launches, it also gets access to Uniswap’s existing distribution through the web app, wallet, API and aggregators.

That could be a serious advantage on a brand-new chain.

And Arc is an interesting place to test it.

USDC is the native gas token. Finality is sub-second. Uniswap v4 is arriving at mainnet, and the first few days will be a fight over who controls token creation, liquidity and discovery.

But there is one major difference between Pools and Pons.

$PONS had a token flywheel.

Pons routed 80% of its protocol share into $PONS buybacks and burns. As launch activity increased, the token became the way to bet on the growth of the launchpad itself.

Pools currently has no equivalent.

Its fees go toward deeper locked liquidity instead of buying a native token.

That is better for traders. Lower fees and deeper liquidity can make Pools more competitive.

But it also creates an interesting problem for investors.

Pools could become the dominant launchpad on Arc while another token captures the speculation around that growth.

So there are really two questions here.

Can Pools become the Pons of Arc?

As infrastructure, it has a strong case. Uniswap Labs, day-one v4 liquidity, 0.25% fees, locked LP and direct access to Uniswap’s distribution is a powerful starting position.

Can it become the next $PONS?

That depends on whether there is ever a token or another mechanism that captures the value created by all that activity.

Without one, Pools can own the flow without having a token that benefits from it.

$PONS became valuable because it became the meter for Robinhood Chain activity.

@TradePools now has the chance to become that meter on Arc.

The product is already sitting in the right seat.

The question is whether anything ends up accruing to the seat.

reason.inference: analytical comparison of PONS model to evaluate new protocol

author: 0xKen__
text:
I love robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571. They have clearly captured the launchpad sector of RH chain and the team keep delivering.

But let's play devil's advocate and address 4 key fundamental questions that doubters may have and that might fill your timeline when the robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 price is down:

1. Launchpad Revenue Sustainability

@ponsdotfamily  has shown explosive growth in the past 2 months. Daily revenue at the start of August was ~$40k and has risen dramatically in the past month, peaking at $1.8 million on 5th September. Since then we have seen revenue pull back and settle at ~$800k - $1m per day.

The ultimate question is: are these numbers sustainable? The buyback of the robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 token is directly linked to these revenue figures.

The answer is directly linked to the future of Robinhood Chain. Attention grew, spiked to coincide with the spike in Pons revenue and has tailed off slightly.

But Pons revenue is STILL way up on where it began. They have swatted off all comers (including Uniswap) and currently account for ~80% of all launchpad volume on the chain.

$1.8 million was a spike, but an average of ~$800k - $1m per day seems to be where the numbers are settling. Still drastically under pricing the robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 token based on xRev compared to solana:pumpCmXqMfrsAkQ5r49WcJnRayYRqmXz6ae8H7H9Dfn.

2. Diversification of Revenue Streams

A major one for the armchair analysts - how many different revenue streams does Pons have? The answer right now is: not very many.

Currently Pons receives fees for token launches (0.0005 ETH), but receives the vast majority of their revenue from swap fees on their own bonding curve and the Uniswap v4 pools that the tokens graduate into.

If volume on the platform reduces, then there are no other revenue streams to fall back to and take up the slack on the token burn that drives the price action on the robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 token.

My answer: we are still incredibly early on Pons' existence, give the team time.

We know that a mobile app is currently under development and the Pons brand is clearly established at this point.

80% of launchpad market capture on Robinhood means a following that can absolutely be pointed at another well executed product.

A Fomo style social trading app? A seamless delegated wallet experience of Pons? Token trading outside the Pons ecosystem? All I know is that the team have consistently delivered and the future is bright - they are just getting started.

3. Token Utility

Currently price action on the robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 token is entirely pushed by a supply side crunch delivered by the token burn. 80% of revenue is used to continuously buy up, and burn, supply from the open market.

This is already a great piece of tokenomics and we have seen the effect so far.

However, could they be doing more?

Using binancecoin:native as an example. When @cz_binance first created the token he set up not only supply side pressure (token burns) but also various elements of DEMAND side pressure to fuel token price action.

Holding binancecoin:native could reduce your fees on a whole host of Binance products and he continued to support it in future products - including integrating it as the gas token on BNB Chain.

What did we see? binancecoin:native went from pennies to thousands of dollars.

Now don't get me wrong, Binance is obviously a much larger beast entirely - but the tokenomics are sound and are absolutely reproducible here.

In my opinion if Pons could integrate some demand side mechanics to increase buying and holding pressure for the token, the sky is truly the limit.

This could play hand in hand with point 2 above and produce one of the greatest flywheels crypto has ever seen.

4. The Future of Robinhood Chain

We touched on this earlier, but it's worth further delving into.

Some people are rightfully questioning whether Robinhood Chain volume will die off as people return to Solana, BNB chain and elsewhere. Has Robinhood season been and gone? Was the initial spike we saw really it?

If volume on the chain dies off, then robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 revenue dries up as well.

In my opinion, it is just getting started.

Robinhood Chain is driving REAL numbers. So far earning ~$42 million in total revenue.

Arbitrum keep 10% of this - but the rest hits the Robinhood balance sheet and directly drives the stock price.

This is a bet that is already showing signs of paying off and @vladtenev is clearly invested in this side of the business.

The chain is complementary to their existing customer base and you can see the synergy in real time as they add Robinhood Chain tokens to the app.

This will only continue and I would not be surprised if we start seeing more Robinhood incubated projects start hitting the chain.

Conclusion

The robinhood:0x39dbed3a2bd333467115de45665cc57f813c4571 token has already seen explosive growth but it is potentially just the tip of the iceberg.

I can see a future where we look back and see it was a very obvious trade in hindsight.
